examples.en: There is a halo around the moon in the night sky tonight.

examples.ko: 달무리가 지면 다음 날 비가 온다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a saying that if the moon has a halo, it rains the next day.
I looked at the halo around the moon outside the window for a long time.
On a night with a halo around the moon, even the wind is gentle.
When I took a photo, the halo around the moon came out big.

examples.ko: 할머니는 달무리를 보고 내일 날씨를 맞히셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother looked at the moon's halo and guessed tomorrow's weather correctly.

explain: 달에 무리(둥근 빛 테두리)가 생기는 현상이고, '달무리가 지다/끼다'처럼 말해요. 해에 생기는 것은 '햇무리'라고 해서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is the ring of light that forms around the moon, and people say '달무리가 지다/끼다'. The same thing around the sun is called '햇무리', so it helps to learn them as a pair.

en: easy and fluent speaking; being glib

examples.ko: 그 사람은 달변이라서 발표를 정말 잘해요.
examples.en: He is such a fluent speaker that he gives really good presentations.
He moved people's hearts with his eloquent speech.
I'm not a smooth talker, but I'll speak sincerely.

examples.ko: 면접에서는 달변보다 솔직함이 더 중요할 때도 있어요.
examples.en: In interviews, honesty is sometimes more important than eloquence.

examples.ko: 친구는 말솜씨가 좋아서 달변이라는 말을 자주 들어요.
examples.en: My friend is good with words, so people often call him eloquent.

examples.ko: 영업 사원이라고 다 달변인 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Not every salesperson is a smooth talker.

explain: '말을 잘하다', '말솜씨가 좋다'가 일상에서는 더 자연스럽고, 달변은 좀 격식 있는 말이에요. 반대말은 '눌변'이고, 사람을 가리킬 때는 '달변가'라고도 해요.
explain_en: In daily talk '말을 잘하다' or '말솜씨가 좋다' sounds more natural, and 달변 is somewhat formal. Its opposite is '눌변', and for a person you can also say '달변가'.

examples.en: Mom hung the garlic under the eaves.

examples.ko: 줄에 종을 달아매면 바람이 불 때 소리가 나요.
examples.en: If you hang a bell on the string, it rings when the wind blows.
I'm hanging radish greens on the wall to dry them.
Please hang the swing firmly on the tree.
I brought a chair to hang the balloons from the ceiling.
Who hung the sign up that high?

explain: 줄이나 끈으로 단단히 묶어서 걸어 놓는 느낌이 있어요. 일상에서는 '매달다'를 더 자주 말하고, '달아매다'는 '달아매요/달아맸어요'처럼 활용해요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of tying something firmly with a rope or string and leaving it hanging. In daily speech '매달다' is used more often, and 달아매다 conjugates as '달아매요/달아맸어요'.

examples.en: The children dashed across the playground.
I ran as fast as I could for fear of missing the bus.
My friend who is quick on his feet came in first.
The puppy saw its owner and came running.
My younger brother is confident in running.
I heard loud running footsteps in the hallway.

explain: '달리기'보다 옛 느낌이 있고 글이나 이야기에서 더 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '뛰어가다', '달려가다'를 많이 써요.
explain_en: It feels more old-fashioned than '달리기' and shows up more in writing and stories. In everyday conversation people usually say '뛰어가다' or '달려가다'.

examples.en: The child saw Mom and dashed over.

examples.ko: 소나기가 오자 사람들이 처마 밑으로 달음박질쳤어요.
examples.en: When the shower started, people dashed under the eaves.
I'm dashing to the station so I don't miss the last train.
The puppy is darting toward the ball.
I fell while dashing and hurt my knee.

examples.ko: 숨이 차도록 달음박질쳐서 겨우 시간에 맞췄어요.
examples.en: I ran until I was out of breath and barely made it on time.

explain: 힘껏 빠르게 뛰어가는 모습을 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '뛰어가다'가 더 흔하고, 활용은 '달음박질쳐요/달음박질쳤어요'처럼 해요.
explain_en: It describes running somewhere quickly with all your strength. In daily talk '뛰어가다' is more common, and it conjugates as '달음박질쳐요/달음박질쳤어요'.

examples.en: Grandmother is brewing herbal medicine.
I boil the medicinal herbs for about two hours.
She boiled ginger for me, saying it's good for colds.

examples.ko: 보약을 달인 물을 하루에 세 번 마셔요.
examples.en: I drink the brewed tonic three times a day.
The longer you boil down soy sauce, the thicker it gets.

examples.ko: 엄마는 매년 겨울에 도라지를 달여 주세요.
examples.en: Every winter, Mom boils down bellflower root for me.

explain: 한약이나 약재, 간장처럼 물이나 액체를 오래 끓여 진하게 만들 때 써요. 소리가 '다리다(옷을 다리다)'와 같아서 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 글자는 '달이다'예요. '세 달이에요'의 '달이에요'는 '달(month)+이에요'라서 이 동사와 달라요.
explain_en: It is used when you boil herbs, medicine or something like soy sauce for a long time to make it concentrated. It sounds the same as '다리다' (to iron clothes), so be careful with the spelling. The '달이에요' in '세 달이에요' is '달' (month) + '이에요', a different thing from this verb.

examples.en: This sweet potato is pleasantly sweet, so it's good as a snack.
A mildly sweet taste lingered in my mouth.
The sikhye is nicely sweet and tasty.
Jujube tea is gently sweet and has a nice aroma.
Please make the sauce a little sweet.
The syrup is slightly sweet but not greasy.

explain: '달콤하다'보다 살짝, 은근하게 단 맛에 어울려요. 비슷한 말로 '달짝지근하다'도 있어요.
explain_en: Compared with '달콤하다', it fits a taste that is slightly or subtly sweet. '달짝지근하다' is a similar word.

examples.en: Sound is turned into signals in the cochlea.
The cochlea is located deep inside the ear.

examples.ko: 사고로 달팽이관을 다쳐서 잘 못 들어요.
examples.en: I hurt my cochlea in an accident, so I can't hear well.

examples.ko: 달팽이관이 손상되면 청력이 떨어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the cochlea is damaged, hearing can decline.
We made a model of the cochlea in science class.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 달팽이관 검사를 받아 보자고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor suggested we do a cochlea test.

explain: 귀 안쪽에서 소리를 느끼는 부분이고, 달팽이 껍데기처럼 돌돌 말린 모양이라 이런 이름이 붙었어요. 과학이나 병원에서 쓰는 말이고, 일상에서는 그냥 '귀 속'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the part deep inside the ear that senses sound, named for its coiled shape like a snail shell. It is used in science and at hospitals, while in daily talk people just say '귀 속' (inside the ear).

en: a little longer than a month; about a month

examples.en: It has been a little over a month since I moved.
I met that friend about a month ago.
The trip seems like it will take about a month.
I was in the hospital for as long as a month.

examples.ko: 아기가 태어난 지 달포밖에 안 됐어요.
examples.en: The baby has been born for only about a month.
The construction finished in about a month.

explain: 딱 한 달이 아니라 '한 달 남짓'이라는 느낌이라서 '달포쯤', '달포 만에'처럼 써요. 앞에 숫자를 붙이지 않아요. 일상 대화에서는 '한 달 정도'라고 많이 말하고, 달포는 글이나 어르신 말투에서 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means a little over a month rather than exactly one, and is used as '달포쯤' or '달포 만에'. You do not put a number in front of it. In daily talk people often say '한 달 정도', and 달포 is heard in writing or from older speakers.

en: good handwriting; person with good penmanship

examples.en: The teacher is famous for beautiful handwriting.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 글씨를 잘 써서 달필이에요.
examples.en: That friend writes very well; he has fine handwriting.

examples.ko: 달필인 사람이 쓴 편지는 읽기도 좋아요.
examples.en: A letter written by someone with fine handwriting is pleasant to read.

examples.ko: 아버지는 달필이라서 축하 글을 자주 부탁받으세요.
examples.en: My father has fine handwriting, so he is often asked to write congratulatory messages.

examples.ko: 저는 달필은 아니지만 또박또박 쓰려고 해요.
examples.en: I don't have fine handwriting, but I try to write neatly.

examples.ko: 달필이 아니어도 정성이 담긴 카드는 좋아요.
examples.en: Even without fine handwriting, a card written with care is lovely.

explain: 글씨를 잘 쓰는 것, 또는 그런 사람을 말해요. 반대말은 '악필'이에요. 보통 대화에서는 '글씨를 잘 쓰다'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to writing well by hand, or to a person who does. Its opposite is '악필' (poor handwriting). In ordinary conversation people more often say '글씨를 잘 쓰다'.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 운동장에서 닭싸움을 자주 했어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I often played chicken fight on the playground.

examples.ko: 닭싸움에서 진 사람이 간식을 사기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided that whoever loses the chicken fight buys the snacks.
I wanted to play chicken fight, so I called my friends.
I sprained my ankle while playing chicken fight.
Do kids these days know chicken fight too?
In chicken fight, a light kid has the advantage.

explain: 실제 닭끼리의 싸움을 뜻하기도 하지만, 말할 때는 한 발로 서서 서로 밀치는 아이들 놀이를 가리킬 때가 많아요. 문맥을 보면 어느 쪽인지 알 수 있어요.
explain_en: It can mean a fight between actual chickens, but in conversation it often refers to the children's game where you stand on one leg and push each other. The context tells you which one is meant.

examples.en: A knife becomes hard through tempering.

examples.ko: 이번 시즌을 앞두고 선수들이 혹독한 담금질에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: Ahead of this season, the players started harsh, toughening training.

examples.ko: 어려운 시기가 오히려 저에게 담금질이 됐어요.
examples.en: The hard times actually toughened me up.

examples.ko: 담금질 과정에서 열을 잘 조절해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to control the heat well during the tempering process.
That time was a tempering of my heart.
The coach made the team strong through rigorous training.

explain: 원래는 뜨겁게 달군 쇠를 물에 넣어 단단하게 하는 일인데, 힘든 훈련이나 경험으로 사람을 단련한다는 비유로도 많이 써요. 스포츠 뉴스에서 '담금질에 들어가다'라는 표현을 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: Originally it is the process of heating metal and plunging it into water to harden it, but it is also widely used figuratively for toughening a person through hard training or experience. In sports news you often see the expression '담금질에 들어가다'.

examples.en: The blacksmith tempers the blade.
The players trained their bodies hard all winter.
I want to steel my mind until the exam.

examples.ko: 쇠를 뜨겁게 달군 뒤 물에 담금질하면 단단해져요.
examples.en: If you heat iron and temper it in water, it becomes hard.
The team has honed its skills through sweat.
I think failure toughened me up.

explain: 쇠를 단단하게 만드는 일뿐 아니라 몸, 마음, 실력을 단련한다는 뜻으로도 널리 써요. 비슷한 말로 '단련하다'가 있는데, 담금질하다는 힘든 과정을 거친다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: Besides hardening metal, it is widely used for training the body, mind or skills. A similar word is '단련하다', but 담금질하다 gives a stronger sense of going through a tough process.

examples.ko: 담력이 큰 아이라서 밤길도 무서워하지 않아요.
examples.en: He is a gutsy kid, so he isn't afraid of night roads.
I tested my nerve on the scary rides at the amusement park.

examples.ko: 담력을 키우려고 일부러 사람들 앞에서 노래했어요.
examples.en: To build up my nerve, I sang in front of people on purpose.

examples.ko: 그는 담력 하나는 누구에게도 안 져요.
examples.en: When it comes to guts, he loses to no one.

examples.ko: 캠프에서 담력 훈련으로 밤길을 혼자 걸었어요.
examples.en: At camp, we walked a night path alone as a nerve-training activity.

examples.ko: 담력 없는 사람은 공포 영화를 못 봐요.
examples.en: People without nerve can't watch horror movies.

explain: 겁내지 않고 버티는 마음의 힘이에요. '용기'보다 무서운 상황에서 겁먹지 않는 느낌이 강하고, 비슷한 말로 '배짱'이 있어요. '담력이 세다/크다', '담력 훈련'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the inner strength to hold steady without fear. Compared with '용기', it leans toward not getting scared in frightening situations, and '배짱' is a similar word. It is used as '담력이 세다/크다' or '담력 훈련'.

examples.en: You need collateral to get a loan from the bank.
I put up my house as collateral and borrowed money.

examples.ko: 담보물의 가치가 떨어지면 대출이 어려워질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the value of the collateral drops, getting a loan can become difficult.

examples.ko: 빚을 갚지 못하면 담보물을 처분할 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you can't repay the debt, the collateral may be sold off.

examples.ko: 담보물 없이 빌릴 수 있는 대출도 있어요.
examples.en: There are also loans you can get without collateral.
I submitted the list of collateral to the bank.

explain: '담보'는 빚을 갚을 수 있다는 보장 자체를 말하고, '담보물'은 그 보장으로 실제로 맡기는 물건(집, 땅 등)을 가리켜요. 은행 대출이나 금융 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '담보' refers to the guarantee itself that a debt will be repaid, while '담보물' is the actual item (a house, land, etc.) put up for it. It often appears in bank loans and financial news.

examples.en: The child filled the rice bowl to the brim.

examples.ko: 엄마가 사랑을 담뿍 담아 편지를 보냈어요.
examples.en: Mom sent a letter filled with love.
Sunlight settled thickly over the flower bed.
I poured milk into the cup until it was full.
I gave the flower bed plenty of water.
I walked down a road piled deep with snow.

explain: 가득, 넉넉하게 차 있는 모양을 말해요. '듬뿍'과 뜻이 비슷하고, 사랑, 정, 햇살처럼 마음이나 자연의 것에도 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes something being full or filled generously. Its meaning is close to '듬뿍', and it also goes well with feelings or nature, such as love, affection and sunlight.

examples.ko: 요즘 동생은 공부와 담쌓고 게임만 해요.
examples.en: These days my brother has given up on studying and only plays games.

examples.ko: 친구와 담쌓은 지 벌써 일 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has already been a year since I cut ties with my friend.
Shutting each other out won't solve the problem.
Why do you live cut off from your family?

examples.ko: 책과 담쌓았던 아이가 이제는 도서관에 가요.
examples.en: The kid who used to want nothing to do with books now goes to the library.
Once you cut someone off, it's hard to get close again.

explain: '~와 담쌓다'는 어떤 사람이나 일과 관계를 끊거나 아예 가까이하지 않는다는 비유로 써요. 실제로 담을 만드는 뜻일 때는 '담을 쌓다'처럼 띄어 써요. '공부랑 담쌓았다'는 말은 공부를 안 한다는 뜻으로 일상에서 자주 해요.
explain_en: '~와 담쌓다' is a figurative expression meaning to cut ties with a person or to stay away from something entirely. When you literally build a wall, it is written separately as '담을 쌓다'. People often say '공부랑 담쌓았다' in daily life to mean someone doesn't study at all.

examples.en: Ivy is climbing up along the wall.

examples.ko: 가을이 되면 담쟁이덩굴 잎이 빨갛게 물들어요.
examples.en: In autumn, the ivy leaves turn red.
The school wall is covered with ivy.
Ivy grows by clinging to walls.
I planted ivy by the window and it grew quickly.

examples.ko: 저는 담쟁이덩굴처럼 끈기 있게 올라가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to keep climbing persistently like ivy.

explain: 벽이나 담을 타고 올라가며 자라는 식물이에요. 줄여서 '담쟁이'라고도 말하고, 오래된 건물이나 학교 벽의 풍경을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a plant that grows by climbing walls and fences. It is also shortened to '담쟁이', and it often appears when describing the scenery of old buildings or school walls.

examples.ko: 간에서 만들어진 담즙은 지방 소화를 도와요.
examples.en: Bile made in the liver helps digest fat.

examples.ko: 담즙이 부족하면 기름진 음식이 소화가 잘 안 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If there isn't enough bile, greasy food may be hard to digest.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 담즙 검사 결과를 설명해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor explained the results of the bile test.
My stomach was so upset that I even threw up bile.
The gallbladder is the organ that stores bile.

examples.ko: 담즙 분비가 줄면 소화에 문제가 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If bile secretion decreases, digestion problems can occur.

explain: 과학이나 의학에서 쓰는 말이고, 일상에서는 '쓸개즙'이라고도 해요. 쓴맛이 나는 소화액이라서 속이 안 좋을 때 쓴 물이 올라오는 얘기에도 나와요.
explain_en: It is a term used in science and medicine, and in daily life people also say '쓸개즙'. Because it is a bitter digestive fluid, it comes up when people talk about bitter liquid rising when they feel sick.

examples.en: I have to meet the boss in person and settle it.

examples.ko: 두 대표는 밤새 담판한 끝에 합의했어요.
examples.en: The two representatives reached an agreement after negotiating all night.
I went to have it out with the landlord over the rent.
This time he said he would settle it once and for all, and he went and did it.

examples.ko: 가격이 맞지 않으면 담판해서라도 깎을 거예요.
examples.en: If the price doesn't fit, I'll bargain hard to get it lowered.

examples.ko: 담판하면 문제가 풀릴 줄 알았는데 쉽지 않았어요.
examples.en: I thought a face-to-face showdown would solve it, but it wasn't easy.

explain: '협상하다'보다 마주 앉아 결판을 짓는 느낌이 강해요. '담판을 짓다', '담판을 벌이다'처럼 명사 형태로도 자주 쓰고, 뉴스나 이야기에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Compared with '협상하다', it feels stronger, like sitting face to face to settle things for good. It is often used in noun form too, as in '담판을 짓다' or '담판을 벌이다', and appears a lot in news and stories.

examples.en: The companies' price collusion was in the news.
The Fair Trade Commission is investigating suspected collusion.
Prices went up because of collusion.
Bid rigging is prohibited by law.

examples.ko: 소비자는 담합 때문에 비싼 값을 내야 했어요.
examples.en: Consumers had to pay high prices because of collusion.

examples.ko: 몇몇 회사가 담합을 했다는 의혹이 있어요.
examples.en: There are suspicions that a few companies colluded.

explain: 뉴스나 경제 이야기에서 '가격 담합', '입찰 담합'처럼 자주 나와요. 몰래 짜고 하는 나쁜 뉘앙스가 있어서 '합의'나 '협의'와는 달라요.
explain_en: It appears often in news and economics as '가격 담합' (price fixing) or '입찰 담합' (bid rigging). It carries a bad nuance of secretly conspiring, so it is different from neutral words like '합의' or '협의'.

examples.en: Suspicions emerged that the companies colluded on prices.
The students conspired together and told a lie.

examples.ko: 업체들이 몰래 담합하면 소비자만 손해를 봐요.
examples.en: If companies secretly collude, only consumers lose out.
There is a company that was caught colluding in a bid.
Their stories were identical, as if the two had conspired.
They claim they did not collude with each other.

explain: 둘 이상이 몰래 미리 짜고 같은 행동을 한다는 나쁜 뉘앙스로 써요. 뉴스에서는 회사들의 가격이나 입찰 이야기가 많고, 평범한 합의에는 '합의하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It carries a bad nuance of two or more parties secretly planning in advance to act the same way. In the news it mostly concerns companies' prices or bids, and for ordinary agreement you use '합의하다'.

examples.en: The president released a statement yesterday.
The statement contains the government's position.
The prime minister's statement was broadcast.
I read the full text of the statement in the newspaper.
Opinions were divided over the content of the statement.
We had a class on writing statements at school.

explain: 정부나 기관이 공식 입장을 알리려고 낸 글을 말하고, 주로 뉴스에서 '담화문을 발표하다'로 나와요. '담화'는 말로 하는 이야기도 포함하지만, 담화문은 글로 된 문서라는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It refers to a written text issued by a government or organization to announce its official position, and mostly appears in the news as '담화문을 발표하다'. '담화' can include spoken talk, but 담화문 is a written document.

examples.en: A return visit is scheduled for next month.
Expectations are high for the leader's return visit.
The schedule for the return visit hasn't been set yet.

examples.ko: 지난번 방문에 대한 답방으로 우리 집에 오셨어요.
examples.en: They came to our house as a return visit for our last visit.
When might a return visit be possible?

examples.ko: 두 나라는 답방 형식으로 교류를 이어 갔어요.
examples.en: The two countries continued exchanges through reciprocal visits.

explain: 방문을 받았던 쪽이 답례로 상대를 다시 찾아가는 일이에요. 주로 외교나 정상회담 뉴스에서 나오고, 일상에서는 '놀러 가다', '찾아가다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is when the side that received a visit goes to see the other side in return. It mostly appears in diplomacy and summit news, and in daily life people say things like '놀러 가다' or '찾아가다'.

examples.en: The negotiations have been at a standstill for months.
Sales are stagnant, so we need a new strategy.
If the economy stagnates, it's hard for jobs to increase too.

examples.ko: 두 나라 관계가 답보하다가 다시 움직이기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Relations between the two countries stalled, then started moving again.
You shouldn't give up just because your grades are stuck.
Because construction stalled, moving in was delayed.

explain: 발전 없이 같은 자리에 머무른다는 뜻으로, 뉴스에서는 '답보 상태에 빠지다'라는 형태로 더 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '제자리걸음이다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means staying in the same place without progress, and in the news it more often appears in the form '답보 상태에 빠지다'. In daily conversation '제자리걸음이다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: I replied as soon as I got the email.
I'm sorry I couldn't reply because I was busy.
The singer personally replied to the fan letter.
I'll definitely reply by tomorrow.
It's important to reply to inquiries politely.
I'll let you know right away when they reply.

explain: '답장하다'가 일상에서 더 흔하고, 답신하다는 이메일이나 공식 문서에 답하는 격식 있는 말이에요. '답신이 오다/보내다'처럼 명사로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: '답장하다' is more common in daily life, while 답신하다 is a more formal word for replying to emails or official documents. It is also often used as a noun, as in '답신이 오다/보내다'.
